items.item: Sections 3 to 10 of the build brief. The brief supplied to the build team stops after Section 2 (Inputs) and then jumps, by reference only, to Sections 11 and 12. Everything between is missing: document architecture, tone and house style, the compliance-matrix format, the cost-model rules, the annex plan and any instruction on what EY wants argued. Needed: the complete brief, or written confirmation that the reconstructed working assumptions recorded in work/analysis/governance.json stand.
items.why: The build is currently running on inferred requirements. Any instruction in the missing sections that contradicts the reconstruction means rework of both documents rather than an edit, and rework is expensive at this stage because the five-page cap forces trade-offs across every section.
items.dueBy: CP-1, scope, compliance and bid shape confirmed

items.item: Section 11 of the brief, the partner review checkpoints. Needed: for each checkpoint, what Michael reviews, what he decides, what the checkpoint blocks until signed, and the order. Six checkpoints (CP-1 to CP-6) have been reconstructed in work/analysis/governance.json as a default; they need to be confirmed, corrected or replaced.
items.why: Sign-off is part of the definition of done. Without the real checkpoint definitions, checkpoint approvals are being given against a standard EY invented rather than the one the brief set, and the build cannot demonstrate that each stage was reviewed as required.
items.dueBy: CP-1, scope, compliance and bid shape confirmed

items.item: Section 12 of the brief, the QA checks both PDFs must pass. items.dueBy: CP-1, scope, compliance and bid shape confirmed

clarificationQuestionsToCI: Submission logistics: what is the deadline for proposals, by what method and to which email address or portal must they be submitted, who is the point of contact for questions, by when must clarification questions be lodged, and what proposal validity period does CI require? The copy of RFP 0032026 we hold begins at Section 2, so none of this is in our pack.
Could CI please supply the complete RFP pack, including Section 1 and any annexes, forms or templates referenced in it? We want to be certain we are not missing a mandatory submission item.

The 'Level of Effort and Cost of Services' section in our copy ends mid-sentence at 'This assignment is expected to be largely desk-based with virtual'. Could CI supply the complete section? It may specify a required level of effort, a number of consultant days, a prescribed LOE table format or constraints on virtual engagement, all of which would change both our technical and cost proposals.

When does CI expect the contract to be signed? All four deliverable dates run from signature, and we would like to confirm whether the 12 weeks span the December and January period, which would affect the availability of the secretariats and tourism boards we intend to interview.

Does the 'max 5 pages (excluding annexes)' cap apply only to Part 1, or to the whole technical proposal including Parts 2 and 3? Do a cover page, contents page and compliance cross-reference table count towards it? Is there any page limit or format specification for the annexes?
Part 1 asks for relevant services undertaken in the past five years, while evaluation criterion 2.2 scores relevant services provided in the last three years. Which window governs the scoring?

Criterion 1.2 reads 'Demonstrate relevant experience to undertake the given assignment (5-10 years)'. Does this mean the firm must show five to ten years of continuous track record in this field, that cited assignments must fall within a five to ten year lookback, or that named key staff must each hold five to ten years of relevant experience? At 20 marks it is the highest-weighted technical criterion, so the reading matters.
The evaluation table runs from criterion 2.2 to criterion 2.4 with no 2.3. The weights sum correctly to 70, but could CI confirm there is no omitted criterion that bidders are expected to address?

Criterion 2.2 requires samples of work delivered. What form and volume does CI expect, and how should commercial confidentiality be handled? Specifically, are redacted extracts acceptable, and do samples count against any page limit?

The submission requirements table includes an 'Other:' line that is blank in our copy. Could CI confirm whether any further item is required, for example company registration documents, a tax clearance certificate, audited financial statements or insurance certificates?

Will CI supply the Offeror Representation of Transparency, Integrity, Social Responsibility template? It is listed as a required submission item but is not in the pack we hold. Does CI require a wet signature, a scanned signature or a qualified electronic signature?
Does CI require the contractor to hold professional indemnity or public liability insurance at specified levels, and must certificates of currency accompany the proposal?

Which Conservation International legal entity and jurisdiction will sign and pay under this contract? If CI contracts through an African country office rather than its US headquarters, domestic withholding tax on non-resident professional fees may apply, which under an all-inclusive price would be absorbed by the supplier and therefore needs to be known before we fix our price.

What is CI's tax position for this engagement? Will CI provide a tax exemption or withholding certificate, is withholding expected to be deducted from payments to a South African supplier, and how should South African VAT on exported services be treated inside the all-inclusive price? At a US$40,000 ceiling this is material.

What are CI's payment terms and invoicing mechanics: days to pay from written acceptance of each deliverable, the invoicing entity and address, whether payment is made in USD by international transfer, which party bears bank charges, and whether any retention applies to the final milestone?

The financial criterion assesses cost 'inclusive of any applicable tax, reimbursables and travel', yet Section 5 states the assignment is desk-based and requires no travel. Could CI confirm that no travel or reimbursable cost is expected, so that showing zero is read as compliance rather than omission?

How many stakeholder presentations does CI expect under deliverable 3, to which stakeholder groups, over what period, and how many rounds of adaptation follow before the final report? The footnote that 'presentations may need to be made to different stakeholder groups as appropriate' is the single largest scope variable in a fixed price that cannot be revised after submission. We have assumed two virtual sessions convened by CI.

Will CI share the list of 15 prioritised emerging protected areas, with country, managing authority and current tourism status, and when? Activity Two requires the models to be assessed especially for the CI priority areas, which cannot be done properly without it. Also, the background says the 15 areas are in Southern and Eastern Africa and then that they are spread across Southern, Eastern and Western Africa; which is correct?

Would CI be willing to broker introductions to the organisations our research programme depends on, principally the secretariats of Boundless Southern Africa, Africa's Eden Tourism and KAZA, the conservancy associations NRT, NACSO and MMWCA, The Long Run, and Preferred Hotel Group and SLH on hosting terms? None of them publishes the cost or outcome data the assessment needs, so primary contact is the only route to it, and CI's standing would materially improve response rates.

Does CI hold existing tourism or brand diagnostics for the priority areas, including demand, visitation, operator or investment pipeline data? We would rather build on that work than repeat it inside a fixed budget.

Does 'at least three' brand solution models mean three is fully sufficient, or will more than three be scored more highly? This drives how we allocate a fixed budget between depth per model and breadth of options.

Is the Activity Three Terms of Reference expected as a standalone, procurement-ready document or as a chapter of the final report? If standalone, would CI share its own ToR or RFP template so the output is directly usable by CI procurement?

What review period will CI commit to on the week 5 and week 10 drafts, and what happens to the schedule and the payment milestone if CI's review runs longer? Only two weeks separate deliverables 3 and 4, and that window must also absorb the stakeholder presentations and adaptation of the preferred model.

Are interviews or deliverables required in French or Portuguese? Several of the likely priority areas and benchmark sources are Francophone or Lusophone, and translation and interviewer capability would need to be costed before submission.

If bidding in partnership or consortium, must the partner be declared at proposal stage, must the partner also sign the Offeror Representation, and must the three client references cover the partner as well as the prime?

Who owns the intellectual property in the deliverables, and may the supplier reference the assignment publicly or reuse its own prior research afterwards? We ask because we are contributing benchmark research completed at our own cost before this proposal.
Does CI intend to award the subsequent implementation assignments referenced in Section 2, and is there any conflict-of-interest restriction on the supplier of this assignment bidding for that work?

Activity One names Africa's Eden. Two organisations use that name: Africa's Eden Tourism, the Botswana-domiciled regional membership association covering eight southern African countries, and a separate Netherlands-based operator running conservation tourism in Gabon, the Central African Republic and Sao Tome and Principe. Which does CI intend, or both?

Part 1 is capped at five pages yet is also required to contain a detailed reference list showing the scope and magnitude of similar assignments, and the relevant services of the past five years. May those two items be provided in an annex and cross-referenced from Part 1, or must they sit inside the five pages?
